doc.title: Schuller Gunther — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Eye accident, return to New York, and his younger brother
summary: He recounts losing an eye in an accident, the school's high academic level, and that he has a younger brother in film.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Take us from coming back to Germany. I want to go back to this growing up in New York and having all this – you’re in Germany. You’ve learned to play the recorder. You’ve learned to sing Bach. Now your back in New York as an 11-, 12-year­ old kid.

Yeah, 11. By the way, one of the reasons I came back from Germany – I had an accident with my eye. It’s a very gruesome thing, where by accident a knife went into my eye. I have had an artificial eye ever since then. But one more sentence about the school in Germany. Scholastically it was just at such a high level. We had – I had, in second grade, I had French, Latin, geography, and geology. You know what they were doing in American schools? Finger paintings and eating cookies and milk in elementary school.
A younger brother. He went into the film business. Very musical, too.
